official_measurement_examples.name: Safeguarding not extraction presumption
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current NPPF minerals policy says Mineral Safeguarding Areas protect known resources from unnecessary sterilisation while explicitly avoiding a presumption that safeguarded resources will be worked.

official_measurement_examples.name: Consultation-area role
official_measurement_examples.fact: A Mineral Consultation Area is based on safeguarding geography and identifies when a district or borough should consult the Mineral Planning Authority on non-mineral development.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning Data coverage limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Planning Data mineral-safeguarding-area dataset currently reports zero providers and no collected records, so absence from that national schema cannot demonstrate absence of a local MSA.

official_measurement_examples.name: BGS resource limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: BGS mineral-resource data maps geological resources and explicitly does not determine mineral reserves or denote potential extraction areas.

official_measurement_examples.name: Historic permissions limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The BGS 1997-2007 permissions dataset includes extant and non-extant permissions and may include active, inactive, restored or unworked sites, so geometry alone does not prove current operational status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local MSA source priority
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local mineral-plan safeguarding datasets can trigger consultation and policy tests and should not be silently replaced by geological-resource polygons.

official_measurement_examples.name: Coal high-risk assessment
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mining Remediation Authority guidance requires a Coal Mining Risk Assessment for most development in a Development High Risk Area, while a Low Risk Area classification does not guarantee absence of unrecorded mining hazards.

official_measurement_examples.name: Restoration separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mineral restoration and aftercare requirements address worked-land recovery and do not convert an extraction permission or completed restoration into planning permission for a later unrelated development.

core_rules: Mineral Safeguarding Area designation is not permission to extract minerals
Mineral Consultation Area status is a consultation trigger not automatic refusal
absence from the zero-provider Planning Data MSA schema is not evidence no local MSA exists
BGS mineral-resource geometry is not a mineral reserve
BGS mineral-resource geometry is not an extraction permission
historic mineral-permission geometry must retain permission date and current-status uncertainty
local adopted minerals-plan evidence must not be replaced by generic geological mapping
prior extraction policy is conditional and not automatic development permission
coal Development High Risk Area status triggers assessment rather than automatic refusal
coal Development Low Risk Area status is not proof of no mining hazard
mineral planning permission is distinct from environmental permits and protected-species licences
restoration and aftercare obligations are distinct from later land-use permission
mineral rights and surface ownership must not be inferred from resource geometry
minerals compliance does not reserve development capacity or access rights
no parcel mineral clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
